at undskylde.explanation: "At undskylde" means "to apologize", and also "to excuse". The short word "Undskyld" means both "Sorry" and "Excuse me". To say what you are sorry for, use "Jeg undskylder for ..." (I apologize for ...).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **undskylde** for at komme for sent.
sentence.en: I would like to apologize for being late.

en uge.explanation: "En uge" means "a week". Useful phrases are "i næste uge" (next week) and "i denne uge" (this week). Weeks are counted by number: "uge 42" means "week 42".

sentence.da: En **uge** har syv dage.
sentence.en: A week has seven days.

en ugedag.explanation: "En ugedag" means "a day of the week", such as Monday or Friday. It is made from "uge" (week) and "dag" (day). Days of the week start with a small letter in Danish: "mandag" (Monday).

sentence.da: Hvilken **ugedag** er det i dag? Det er tirsdag.
sentence.en: Which day of the week is it today? It is Tuesday.

et udsalg.explanation: "Et udsalg" means "a sale", a time when a shop sells things at lower prices. "Der er udsalg" means "There is a sale".

sentence.da: Jakken var billig, for jeg købte den på **udsalg**.
sentence.en: The jacket was cheap, because I bought it on sale.

et ur.explanation: "Et ur" means "a clock" or "a watch". A watch on your wrist is "et armbåndsur" and a wall clock is "et vægur". Do not mix it up with "klokken", used for telling the time: "Hvad er klokken?" means "What time is it?".

sentence.da: Jeg kigger på mit **ur**, og klokken er ti.
sentence.en: I look at my watch and it is ten o'clock.

forms.en: He goes out of the house.
I go out into the garden.

ud.explanation: "Ud" means "out" and is used when something moves from inside to outside: "Kom ud!" (Come out!). For being outside, Danes say "ude" (outside). "Hvordan ser det ud?" means "What does it look like?".

sentence.da: Solen skinner, så vi går **ud** i haven.
sentence.en: The sun is shining, so we go out into the garden.

uden.explanation: "Uden" means "without". Before an action it is "uden at": "uden at spise" (without eating). Do not mix it up with "udenfor" (outside).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have kaffe **uden** sukker, kun med mælk.
sentence.en: I want coffee without sugar, only with milk.

udenfor.explanation: "Udenfor" means "outside", both for where something is and for going out: "Vi er udenfor" (We are outside) and "Vi går udenfor" (We go outside). It can also be written as two words, "uden for".

sentence.da: Børnene er ikke inde i huset, de leger **udenfor**.
sentence.en: The children are not inside the house, they are playing outside.

udsolgt.explanation: "Udsolgt" means "sold out", with none left to buy. It is made of "ud" (out) and "solgt" (sold).

sentence.da: Der er ikke flere billetter, de er **udsolgt**.
sentence.en: There are no more tickets, they are sold out.

ugift.explanation: "Ugift" means "unmarried", the opposite of "gift" (married). "U-" in front of a word often makes its opposite, as in "uvenlig" (unfriendly), the opposite of "venlig" (friendly).

sentence.da: Han har ingen kone, han er **ugift**.
sentence.en: He has no wife, he is unmarried.

ukraine.explanation: "Ukraine" means "Ukraine", spelled just as in English. Countries take "i" for being there and "til" for going there: "Jeg bor i Ukraine" (I live in Ukraine).

sentence.da: Kyiv er en stor by i **Ukraine**.
sentence.en: Kyiv is a big city in Ukraine.

ukrainsk.explanation: "Ukrainsk" means "Ukrainian", for people, things and the language. It is written with a small letter, where English uses a capital.

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Ukraine og taler **ukrainsk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Ukraine and speaks Ukrainian.

under.explanation: "Under" means "under" or "below", and also "during": "under krigen" (during the war). With numbers it means "less than": "under ti" (under ten).

sentence.da: Katten sover **under** sengen.
sentence.en: The cat sleeps under the bed.

underbukser.explanation: "Underbukser" means "underpants". It is built from "under" (under) and "bukser" (pants), and like "bukser" it is usually used in the plural.

sentence.da: Jeg tager mine **underbukser** på, og så mine bukser.
sentence.en: I put on my underpants, and then my pants.

undertøj.explanation: "Undertøj" means "underwear". It is built from "under" (under) and "tøj" (clothes). Like "tøj", it covers the whole category, so you do not count it: "nyt undertøj" (new underwear).

sentence.da: Jeg tager rent **undertøj** på, før jeg tager bukser og trøje på.
sentence.en: I put on clean underwear before I put on pants and a sweater.

forms.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

undskyld.explanation: "Undskyld" means both "sorry" and "excuse me". You use it to apologise, as in "Undskyld, jeg kom for sent" (Sorry, I came too late), and to get someone's attention politely, as in "Undskyld, må jeg komme forbi?" (Excuse me, may I get past?). Said as a question, "Undskyld?" means "Pardon?" when you did not hear.

sentence.da: **Undskyld**, hvor er toilettet?
sentence.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

forms.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

undskyld mig.explanation: "Undskyld mig" means "excuse me" and is used to get someone's attention or to pass by. Danes often shorten it to just "undskyld", which can also mean "sorry".

sentence.da: **Undskyld mig**, må jeg komme forbi?
sentence.en: Excuse me, may I get past?

ung.explanation: "Ung" means "young". "De unge" (literally "the young ones") means "young people". For a baby or small child Danes usually say "et barn" (a child) or "lille" (little) rather than "ung".

sentence.da: Hun er kun femten år, så hun er meget **ung**.
sentence.en: She is only fifteen years old, so she is very young.

usa.explanation: "USA" means "the USA". You say "Jeg bor i USA" (I live in the USA), with no word for "the". It is said letter by letter, "u-es-a".

sentence.da: New York ligger i **USA**.
sentence.en: New York is in the USA.

usund.explanation: "Usund" means "unhealthy". It is built from "u" (un-) and "sund" (healthy), like "uvenlig" (unfriendly). It is used for food, habits and lifestyles.

sentence.da: Slik og kage er **usund** mad, men frugt er sund.
sentence.en: Candy and cake are unhealthy food, but fruit is healthy.
